title: The suffering servant is not the whole people
source_text: Μέμνημαι δέ ποτε ἔν τινι πρὸς τοὺς λεγομένους παρὰ Ἰουδαίοις σοφοὺς [ἐν]ζητήσει ταῖς προφητείαις ταύταις χρησάμενος, ἐφ᾿ οἷς ἔλεγεν ὁ Ἰουδαῖος ταῦτα πεπροφητεῦσθαι ὡς περὶ ἑνὸς τοῦ ὅλου λαοῦ, καὶ γενομένου ἐν τῇ διασπορᾷ καὶ πληγέντος, ἵνα πολλοὶ προσήλυτοι γένωνται τῇ προφάσει τοῦ ἐπεσπάρθαι Ἰουδαίους τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσι. καὶ οὕτω διηγεῖτο τὸ „ἀδοξήσει ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπων τὸ εἶδός σου“ καὶ τὸ „οἷς οὐκ ἀνηγγέλη περὶ αὐτοῦ ὄψονται“ καὶ τὸ ἄνθρωπος ἐν πληγῇ ὤν.“ πολλὰ μὲν οὖν τότ᾿ ἐν τῇ ζητήσει λέλεκται τὰ ἐλέγχοντα ὅτι περί τινος ἑνὸς ταῦτα προφητευόμενα οὐκ εὐλόγως ἐκεῖνοι ἀνάγουσιν ἐπὶ ὅλον τὸν λαόν. ἐπυνθανόμην δὲ, τίνος ἂν εἴη πρόσωπον τὸ λέγον· „οὗτος τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν φέρει καὶ περὶ ἡμῶν ὀδυνᾶται“ καὶ τό· „αὐτὸς δὲ ἐτραυματίσθη διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, καὶ μεμαλάκισται διὰ τὰς ἀνομίας ἡμῶν,“ καὶ τίνος πρόσωπον ἦν τὸ φάσκον· „τῷ μώλωπι αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν.“ σαφῶς γὰρ οἱ ἐν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις γενόμενοι καὶ ἰαθέντες ἐκ τοῦ τὸν σωτῆρα πεπονθέναι, εἴτ᾿ ἀπὸ τοῦ λαοῦ ἐκείνου εἴτε καὶ οἱ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν, ταῦτα λέγουσι παρὰ τῷ προφήτῃ προεωρακότι καὶ ἀπὸ ἁγίου πνεύματος ταῦτα προσωποποιήσαντι. μάλιστα δ᾿ ἐδόξαμεν θλίβειν ἀπὸ τῆς φασκούσης λέξεως τό· „ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνομιῶν τοῦ λαοῦ μου ἤχθη εἰς θάνατον.“ εἰ γὰρ ὁ λαὸς κατ᾿ ἐκείνους εἰσὶν οἱ προφητευόμενοι, πῶς „ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνομιῶν τοῦ λαοῦ“ τοῦ θεοῦ λέγεται ἦχθαι „εἰς θάνατον“ οὗτος, εἰ μὴ ἕτερος ὢν παρὰ τὸν λαὸν τοῦ θεοῦ; τίς δ᾿ οὗτος, εἰ μὴ Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς, οὗ „τῷ μώλωπι“ „ἰάθημεν“ οἱ εἰς αὐτὸν πιστεύοντες, ἀπεκδυσαμένου „τὰς“ ἐν ἡμῖν „ἀρχὰς καὶ ἐξουσίας“ καὶ „παῤῥησίᾳ“ δειγματίσαντος αὐτὰς ἐν τῷ ξύλῳ; ἕκαστον δὲ τῶν ἐν τῇ προφητείᾳ σαφηνίσαι καὶ μηδὲν ἀβασάνιστον αὐτῶν παραλιπεῖν ἄλλου καιροῦ ἐστι. καὶ ταῦτα δ᾿ ἐπὶ πλεῖον εἴρηται, ὡς νομίζω, ἀναγκαίως διὰ τὴν ἐκκειμένην τοῦ παρὰ τῷ Κέλσῳ Ἰουδαίου λέξιν.
pass_a_gloss: I remember (μέμνημαι) once in a certain inquiry/debate (ζήτησις) with those called wise (σοφός) among Jews having used (χράομαι) these prophecies (προφητεία); at which the Jew said these had been prophesied (προφητεύω) as about one (εἷς), the whole people (λαός), which came to be in the dispersion (διασπορά) and was struck (πλήσσω), so that many might become proselytes (προσήλυτος) by occasion (πρόφασις) of Jews having been scattered among (ἐπισπείρω) the other nations (ἔθνος). And thus he explained (διηγέομαι) 'your form (εἶδος) will be unhonoured (ἀδοξέω) by men' and 'to whom it was not announced (ἀναγγέλλω) about him, they will see' and 'man being in a stroke (πληγή)'. Many things then in the inquiry were said refuting (ἐλέγχω) that these, prophesied about some one, they unreasonably (οὐκ εὐλόγως) refer (ἀνάγω) to the whole people. I inquired (πυνθάνομαι) whose person/character (πρόσωπον) would be the one saying 'this one bears (φέρω) our sins (ἁμαρτία) and suffers pain (ὀδυνάω) for us' and 'he was wounded (τραυματίζω) because of our sins and has been made weak (μαλακίζομαι) because of our lawless deeds (ἀνομία)', and whose person was the one declaring 'by his bruise (μώλωψ) we were healed (ἰάομαι)'. For clearly those having been in sins and healed from the Saviour (σωτήρ) having suffered (πάσχω), whether from that people or from the nations, say these things in the prophet who foresaw (προοράω) and from the Holy Spirit (ἅγιον πνεῦμα) gave these things speaking characters (προσωποποιέω). Most we seemed to press (θλίβω) from the passage (λέξις) saying 'from the lawless deeds of my people he was led (ἄγω) to death'. For if according to them the people are those prophesied, how is this one said to have been led to death from the lawless deeds of the people of God unless being other (ἕτερος) than the people of God? Who is this unless Jesus Christ, by whose bruise we believing in him were healed, he having stripped off (ἀπεκδύομαι) the rulers and authorities (ἀρχαί, ἐξουσίαι) in us and with boldness/openly (παρρησία) having made an example (δειγματίζω) of them on the tree (ξύλον)? To clarify (σαφηνίζω) each of the things in the prophecy and leave nothing of them unexamined (ἀβασάνιστος) is of another occasion (καιρός). And these things have been said at greater length, as I think, necessarily (ἀναγκαίως) because of the set-out (ἐκκεῖμαι) passage of the Jew in Celsus.
pass_b_english: I remember once using these prophecies in a debate with those whom the Jews call wise. To this the Jew replied that they had been prophesied of the whole people as of a single person, a people that had been in the dispersion and had been struck, so that many might become proselytes through the Jews having been scattered among the other nations. In this way he explained “Your appearance will be without honour among men” (Isaiah 52:14), and “Those who were not told of him will see” (Isaiah 52:15), and “a man under a blow” (Isaiah 53:3).

Many arguments were put forward in that debate to prove that they have no good reason for referring to the whole people these prophecies, which concern one particular person. I asked whose character it could be that says, “This man bears our sins and suffers pain for us” (Isaiah 53:4), and, “But he was wounded because of our sins, and has been made weak because of our lawless deeds” (Isaiah 53:5); and whose character it was that declares, “By his bruise we were healed” (Isaiah 53:5). For plainly it is those who had been in sins and were healed through the Saviour’s suffering, whether they came from that people or from the nations, who say these words in the prophet, who foresaw this and, by the Holy Spirit, put these words in their mouths.

But we seemed to press them hardest with the passage that says, “Because of the lawless deeds of my people he was led to death” (Isaiah 53:8). For if, on their view, it is the people who are the subject of the prophecy, how is this man said to have been led “to death” “because of the lawless deeds of the people” of God, unless he is someone other than the people of God? And who is he, if not Jesus Christ, by whose “bruise” we who believe in him “were healed” (Isaiah 53:5; 1 Peter 2:24), he who stripped off “the rulers and authorities” that were in us, and made a show of them “openly” on the tree (Colossians 2:15)?

To make clear each point in the prophecy, and to leave none of it unexamined, belongs to another occasion. Even this much has been said at some length, necessarily, I think, because of the words of Celsus’s Jew quoted above.

choices.choice: Koetschau brackets ἐν before ζητήσει; read ζητήσει ('in a debate'). The staged text lacks the opening quotation mark before ἄνθρωπος ἐν πληγῇ ὤν; treated as a quotation of Isaiah 53:3 LXX. All Isaiah quotations are Septuagint (LXX and English verse numbers agree in Isaiah 52-53); 'blow' (πληγή), 'bruise' (μώλωψ) and 'made weak' (μεμαλάκισται) follow the LXX wording rather than the Hebrew. In Isaiah 53:5 Origen has 'sins' and 'lawless deeds' in the reverse of the usual LXX order; translated as he quotes it. πρόσωπον / προσωποποιήσαντι are the grammarians' terms for a speaking character: 'whose character it could be that says' and 'put these words in their mouths'. 'Of God' after 'the people' is Origen's gloss on 'my people' (outside his quotation marks). The relative clause οὗ τῷ μώλωπι ἰάθημεν echoes 1 Peter 2:24 (οὗ τῷ μώλωπι ἰάθητε, with ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον), hence the double citation; 'stripped off the rulers and authorities ... openly' is Colossians 2:15, with Origen's own additions 'in us' and 'on the tree' (where Paul has ἐν αὐτῷ). The 'debate' (ζήτησις) is Origen's own disputation with Jewish teachers, not a quotation of Celsus.
'in a debate with some of those whom the Jews call wise' to 'with those whom the Jews call wise' (τινι goes with ζητήσει, 'a certain debate', not with the wise men)
'scattered abroad and struck down' to 'had been in the dispersion and had been struck' (γενομένου ἐν τῇ διασπορᾷ καὶ πληγέντος; 'struck down' overstated)
Isaiah 52:14 'held without honour by men' to 'without honour among men'; Isaiah 52:15 'Those to whom nothing was announced about him' to 'Those who were not told of him'
Isaiah 53:3 'a man under a stroke' to 'a man under a blow' ('stroke' reads as the illness in modern English); note updated
'in their sins' to 'in sins'; 'foresaw these things' to 'foresaw this' (ταῦτα belongs to προσωποποιήσαντι); 'set them in the mouths of these speakers' to 'put these words in their mouths'

'when he stripped off ... and made a public show of them, "openly,"' to 'he who stripped off ... and made a show of them "openly"' (participles agree with οὗ, not a time clause; removed the doubled 'public ... openly')
'set out above' to 'quoted above' (ἐκκειμένην); added a note that Origen reverses 'sins' and 'lawless deeds' in Isaiah 53:5
Checked every Isaiah verse against the LXX (52:14, 52:15, 53:3, 53:4, 53:5, 53:8), 1 Peter 2:24 and Colossians 2:15
